newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's stock market rises in the ratings.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's stock market rises in the ratings.

text.p: Portugal's stock market was promoted on Wednesday to the ranks of the world's developed markets by the U.S. bank Morgan Stanley whose ratings are followed closely by international fund managers.

Portugal, which had previously been classified as an emerging market by Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI), will be included in its developed market index from December 2, 1997, the company said in a statement.
The change marked "recognition of Portugal's overall economic development, its macro-economic and financial policies, as well as its equity market characteristics."
"Its characterisation as emerging is no longer appropriate," it said.

The move, which had long been expected, is likely to give a further boost to interest in the Portuguese market as many international fund managers base their foreign investment strategies on the MSCI indices.
The switch from emerging to developed should bring a significant increase in the weightings they attach to Portugal, analysts said.
Capital International said that Portugal's gross domestic product (GDP), the measure of an economy's output, exceeded the threshold used by the World Bank to categorise high-income countries.
Portugal had also been carrying out structural reforms to its economy and was amongst leading candidates to form part of the European Union's single currency at its launch in 1999, it said.
While the equity market was still modest in size, it had been expanding in terms of capitalisation.
"All the above improvements have positively impacted international investors' confidence," Capital International.

Stock market liquidity has been given a big boost by a series of privatisations and Portugal's Socialist government is planning to float state electricity concern EDP in the summer in what will be the largest state sale yet.
